I know how you feel. It must be really tough, right?
I know how you feel. I've been there too.

description: Promise a friend you will stay by their side for support. Just place a noun before 내가 옆에 있을게 — no conjugation needed. Common uses: 힘들어도 내가 옆에 있을게. (Even when it's tough, I'll be by your side.) or 걱정 마. 내가 옆에 있을게. (Don't worry. I'll be right here with you.).

examples.en: Even when it's tough, I'll be by your side.
Don't worry. I'll be right here with you.
I'll always be by your side.

description: Tease that a story or situation has a surprising twist ending. Say what you need

examples.en: This drama has a twist — it's shocking!
There's a twist? Don't spoil it!
There's a real twist — watch it to the end!

description: Say something leaves a lingering impression long after it ends. Say what you nee

examples.en: This drama leaves a lingering impression.
It leaves a lingering impression — I don't think I'll forget it for a while.
examples.ko: 여운이 남아요, 한동안 못 잊을 것 같아요.

examples.en: It leaves a lingering impression? That's the sign of a good drama!

description: Say you get totally absorbed and lost in something you're doing. Say what you ne

examples.en: This drama is totally immersive!
I got so immersed that I watched it all night!
It's a drama that really draws you in!

description: Describe being inexplicably drawn to something without a clear reason. Say what you need, then add 어딘가 모르게 끌려요 at the end. Common uses: 이 그림, 어딘가 모르게 끌려요. (I'm drawn to this painting for some reason.) or 처음 봤는데 어딘가 모르게 끌려요. (I just saw it, but I'm inexplicably drawn to it.).

examples.en: I'm drawn to this painting for some reason.
I just saw it, but I'm inexplicably drawn to it.
For some reason, I'm drawn to Korean.

description: Express not wanting to leave a place or moment you love. Say what you need, then

examples.en: I don't want to leave Korea — I love it so much!
I don't want to leave — I love it here so much!
I still don't want to leave — I want to stay longer!
examples.ko: 아직 떠나기 싫어, 더 있고 싶어!

description: Anticipate missing something or someone after you leave. Say what you need, then

examples.en: I think I'll miss Jisu!
I think I'll miss Korean food!
I think I'll miss the Han River — it's so beautiful!
examples.ko: 한강이 그리울 것 같아, 너무 예쁘잖아!

description: Make a firm promise to definitely come back to a place. Say what you need, then

examples.en: I'll definitely come back — I promise!
I'll definitely come back — wait for me!
I'll definitely come back to Korea!

description: Mark a fluency milestone: thinking directly in Korean without translating. Just

examples.en: I think in Korean now!
I even dream in Korean now — I think in Korean!
examples.ko: 꿈도 한국어로 꿔요, 이제 한국어로 생각해요!

examples.en: You think in Korean now? That's amazing!

description: Say you now understand Korean directly without needing to translate. Just place

examples.en: I understand without even translating!
I understand without translating now — it's amazing!
examples.ko: 이제 번역 안 해도 이해돼요, 신기해요!

examples.en: You understand without translating? You've really improved!
examples.ko: 번역 안 해도 이해돼요? 완전 늘었네요!

description: Note that someone's ability or skill has grown significantly. Just place a noun

examples.en: My Korean skills have improved a lot!
My skills have improved a lot — I'm glad I didn't give up!
examples.ko: 실력이 많이 늘었어요, 포기 안 하길 잘했어요!

examples.en: Your skills have improved a lot? What's the secret?

description: Reflect that both of you have grown and improved through a shared journey. Say w

examples.en: I feel like we've grown together!
I feel like we grew together while studying together.
examples.ko: 같이 공부하면서 같이 성장한 것 같아요.

examples.en: I feel like we've grown together — thank you!

description: Credit someone for helping you learn or grow a lot. Just place a noun before 덕분에

examples.en: I've learned so much thanks to you!
I've learned so much thanks to all of you!
I've learned so much thanks to you — thank you!

description: Ask how long something takes. Use when waiting, traveling, or estimating time. Say 얼마나 걸려요? after describing the activity.

examples.en: How long does it take?
How long does it take to get home?
How long do I have to wait?

description: ❌ 없음

examples.en: How long does it take to get to Hongdae from here?
How long does delivery take?
How long does ramen take?

description: Used to ask whether someone can eat a certain food, often because it may be spicy or cause an allergy.

examples.en: Can you eat spicy food?
Can you eat seafood?
Can you eat peanuts?

english: I don't know what I should ~.
description: Used when you are unsure what to do, choose, buy, or say.

examples.en: I don't know what I should buy.
I don't know where I should go.
I don't know what I should say.

description: Used to ask whether a food, drink, or product contains a certain ingredient.

examples.en: Does this dish contain meat?
Does it contain milk?
Does it contain peanuts?

description: Used when you realize or decide that you should do something.

examples.en: I should take an umbrella.
I should go now.
I should go to bed early today.

description: Used to say which part of your body hurts.

examples.en: My head hurts.
My stomach hurts.
My throat hurts.

description: Used in casual speech to talk about a completed action or past situation.

examples.en: I watched a movie yesterday.
I met a friend.
I went to the Han River.

description: Used in casual speech to talk about a future plan, prediction, or intention.

examples.en: I'm going tomorrow.
It will rain soon.
I'll call you this evening.

english: I want to make Korean friends.
description: Used to express a desire to make Korean friends.

examples.en: I want to make Korean friends.
I want to make new friends at school.
I want to make friends from different countries.

description: Used to give background information or explain a reason the listener may not know.

examples.en: You see, I'm learning Korean.
I have plans today, you see.
I come to this restaurant often, you see.

english: I noticed that ~. / It turned out that ~.
description: Used to share something you personally noticed or experienced.

examples.en: I found it tastier than expected.
I noticed there were a lot of people.
I found that it was cold at night.

description: Used to offer to do something for another person.

examples.en: I'll help you.
I'll take a picture for you.
I'll tell you later.

description: Used in casual speech to say which person, thing, or activity you like best.

examples.en: I like spring the most.
I like this song the most.
I like bulgogi the most among Korean foods.
examples.ko: 한국 음식 중에는 불고기가 제일 좋아.

description: Used to talk politely about a future plan, intention, or prediction.

examples.en: I'm going to study tomorrow.
I'm going to travel this weekend.
I'm going to Korea next month.

description: Used in casual speech to ask whether someone has tried or experienced something.

examples.en: Have you tried kimchi?
Have you tried wearing hanbok?
Have you been to Jeju Island?

description: Used in casual speech to ask someone to teach or show you how to do something.

examples.en: Can you teach me English?
Can you teach me this dance?
examples.ko: 이 춤 가르쳐 줄 수 있어?

examples.en: Can you show me how to use it?

description: Used to ask how to say something or how to do something.

examples.en: How do you say this in Korean?
How do I order?
How do I use this app?

english: Have you tried ~? / Have you ever done ~?
description: Used to ask politely whether someone has tried or experienced an activity.

examples.en: Have you worked at a café?
Have you traveled alone?
Have you made Korean food?

description: Used to ask about someone's opinion or experience after something happened.

examples.en: How was the trip?
How was your first class?
How was your new job?

description: Used when you decide to try something new or difficult.

examples.en: I'll give it a try too.
I'll try it by myself this time.
I'll give it a try even if it's difficult.

description: Used to give a mild or careful positive opinion without sounding too enthusiastic.

examples.en: This design isn't bad.
The taste isn't bad.
It's not as bad as I expected.

description: Used to politely agree with another person's opinion.

examples.en: I think so too.
That's a good idea. I think so too.
That's right. I think so too.

description: Used to express surprise that something has a quality to such a strong degree.

examples.en: Is spring in Korea this beautiful?
Is this food this spicy?
Is the subway this fast?

english: I like this time the most.
description: Used to say that a certain time, season, or moment is your favorite.

examples.en: I like it most when the cherry blossoms bloom.
I like this time in the morning the most.
I like this cool time of year the most.

description: Used to ask about a topic, option, season, place, or person's opinion.

examples.en: What is summer like?
How is this food?
How about the weekend?

description: Used to admit politely that you made a mistake.

examples.en: It was my fault.
I'm really sorry. It was my fault.
This was my mistake.

description: Used to promise that you will make an effort to do something.

examples.en: I'll try to come early next time.
I'll try to contact you more often.
I'll try to understand the other person.

description: Used to ask where a certain type of trash or item should be discarded.

examples.en: Where do I throw away this bottle?
Where do I throw away food waste?
Where do I throw away paper?

description: Used to ask whether a rule or practice is followed carefully and thoroughly.

examples.en: Do you sort recycling carefully?
Do you manage hygiene strictly?
Do you carry out security checks thoroughly?

description: Used when you realize that you need to be more careful about something.

examples.en: I should pay more attention to recycling.
I should pay more attention to my health.
I should pay more attention to my pronunciation.

description: Used when you feel excited or pleasantly nervous without knowing exactly why.

examples.en: Something feels exciting today.
I feel excited because it's the day before the trip.
Being here makes me feel excited.

description: Used to express appreciation for a meaningful or special moment.

examples.en: Moments like this are precious.
Moments like this with friends are precious.
It's ordinary, but moments like this are precious.

english: I think there was a misunderstanding.
description: Used to gently explain that people may have misunderstood each other.

examples.en: I think there was a misunderstanding between us.
examples.ko: 우리 사이에 오해가 있었던 것 같아요.

examples.en: I think there was a misunderstanding about what I said.
examples.ko: 제 말에 오해가 있었던 것 같아요.

examples.en: I think we misunderstood each other.

description: Used to clarify that your words or actions were understood differently from what you intended.

examples.en: I didn't mean that.
I didn't mean to ignore you.
I didn't mean to get angry.

description: Used to reassure someone that you understand their feelings or situation.

examples.en: I completely understand what you mean.
I completely understand how you feel.
I fully understand the situation.

description: Used to say that not doing something was the right decision.

examples.en: I'm glad I didn't give up.
I'm glad I didn't cancel the plan.
I'm glad I didn't leave too early.

english: Once you understand it, it is ~.
description: Used to say that something is different or easier after you understand it better.

examples.en: Korean is easy once you understand it.
This rule is simple once you understand it.
That person is kind once you get to know them.

description: Used to ask how two things, words, or ideas are different.

examples.en: What is the difference between these two words?
What is the difference between polite and casual speech?
What is the difference between these two menu items?

description: Used to emphasize the most important part of an explanation.

examples.en: This is the key point.
This is the key point in pronunciation.
This part is the most important. This is the key point.
examples.ko: 이 부분이 가장 중요해요. 이게 포인트예요.

description: Used to admit that you want something while suggesting there is a concern or contrast.

examples.en: I do want to stay in Korea longer, though.
I do want to go together, though.
I do want to buy it, though.

description: Used to state what you plan to do for a goal, person, or purpose.

examples.en: I will study hard for my dream.
I will exercise for my health.
I will do my best for my family.

description: Used to mention information you heard from another person or source.

examples.en: I heard that this restaurant is good.
I heard that it will rain tomorrow.
I heard that the movie is interesting.

english: I heard that ~. / I found out that ~.
description: Used to pass along something you heard or learned, often with a sense of discovery.

examples.en: I heard that café is good.
I heard that it's crowded on weekends.
I heard that Korean winters are cold.

english: I didn't know that ~ would/could happen.
description: Used to express surprise about something you did not expect or know.

examples.en: I didn't know it would be this delicious.
I didn't know there would be so many people.
I didn't know I would be able to have a conversation in Korean.
examples.ko: 한국어로 대화할 수 있을 줄 몰랐어요.

description: Used to ask whether an event or situation happens often.

examples.en: Is this kind of thing common?
Is it common for the subway to be late?
Is heavy snow common in winter?
examples.ko: 겨울에 눈이 많이 오는 게 흔한 일이에요?

english: It is much more ~ than expected.
description: Used to emphasize that something is far beyond what you expected.

examples.en: It's much tastier than I expected.
It's much closer than I expected.
It's much harder than I expected.

description: Used to express a negative or hesitant opinion in a softer, more polite way.

examples.en: The design is a little questionable, though.
The price is a bit much, though.
The taste isn't quite for me, though.

english: I can't say that's not true.
description: Used to partly agree with a statement, even if you do not agree completely.

examples.en: I can't say that's not true.
I can't say it isn't expensive.
examples.ko: 비싸다는 말을 아니라고 할 순 없죠.

examples.en: I can't deny that it's a little difficult.
examples.ko: 조금 어렵다는 건 아니라고 할 순 없죠.

description: Used to politely say that a general statement is not true in every situation.

examples.en: That's not always the case.
Not all Korean food is spicy.
examples.ko: 한국 음식이 모두 매운 건 아니에요.

examples.en: Expensive things are not always good.

english: Try thinking from the other person's point of view.
description: Used to advise someone to consider another person's feelings or situation.

examples.en: Try thinking from the other person's point of view.
Try thinking from your friend's point of view.
Try thinking from your parents' point of view too.

description: Used to comfort someone and promise to support them.

examples.en: I'll be by your side.
I'll be by your side when things are hard.
Don't worry. I'll be by your side.

description: Used to say that a journey, goal, or new stage has only just started.

examples.en: My Korean studies are just beginning.
My new challenge is just beginning.
My life in Korea is just beginning.

english: I will achieve my dream through ~.
description: Used to say what skill, method, or path you will use to achieve your dream.

examples.en: I will achieve my dream through Korean.
I will achieve my dream through music.
I will achieve my dream through steady effort.

description: Used to say that a journey, story, activity, or relationship is continuing.

examples.en: The Korean journey continues.
Our story continues.
Learning continues.
